family: Online portfolio selection (Cover 1991 universal portfolios, EG, ONS, follow-the-leader), mean-reversion OLPS (PAMR/OLMAR/CWMR/RMR), transaction-cost-aware OLPS (Blum–Kalai, TCO), and regret-minimisation (Hedge/EWA, Fixed-Share, EXP3/EXP4) over a finite set of expert TACTICS (trend book, reversal book, constant-mix, flat).
thesis: The tactic is to stop learning a forecast and instead run K closed-form books (trend30 = the frozen 819 rule, its long-flat variant, a short-horizon reversal book, the uniform constant-rebalanced long basket, flat, optionally an alt-vs-BTC constant-mix) and let a regret-minimising meta-rule (Hedge/EWA, Fixed-Share, follow-the-leader, or Cover's UP over the experts' price relatives) move a fully visible weight vector on the K-simplex by cumulative realised net@21 losses; "hold on policy" is then literal — the action space is K numbers, every move is explained by a loss ledger, and turnover of the meta layer is bounded by the learning rate. Where the profit comes from must be stated per member: (a) Hedge/UP/FTL over experts has NO profit source of its own — the guarantee is a bound on shortfall versus the best expert (or best constant mixture) in hindsight, so the meta inherits the experts' sources (trend and reversal books are FORECASTS, source 1; flat is zero); (b) PAMR/OLMAR/CWMR are forecasts dressed as tactics (they predict x̂_{t+1} = 1/x_t or MA_t/x_t and trade aggressively on it; Li–Hoi 2014 §PAMR/CWMR: "no meaningful theoretical regret bound") with unbounded turnover — the opposite of holding; (c) the only intrinsic non-forecast source in the family is the constant-rebalanced portfolio's excess growth rate, ½(Σwσ_i² − σ_p²) (source 3, rebalancing premium), which on this panel is worth ≈0.16/yr ≈ +0.27 Sharpe-equivalent on top of a long-only basket whose measured Sharpe is −0.37 FULL and −2.49 in 2022 (the scorer's `bh` column is exactly that UCRP). (d) Mixing opposite books nets trades inside the combined position matrix — a real source-4 cost reduction, automatically captured if the mixture is scored as one book. Net: the family is a control/audit layer, not an edge; its expected profit is bounded above by the best fixed convex mixture of the experts minus regret, and the experts already in the record cap that hull near +0.1 net@21 over 2024–2026H1.
math: (1) Cover UP (Dirichlet(½) prior, Cover–Ordentlich 1996 Thm 2): ln(W_BCRP/W_UP) ≤ ((m−1)/2)·ln(T+1) + ln 2. m=6 experts, T=365: 15.4 nats (wealth factor e^15.4 ≈ 5·10^6); m=64 assets, T=365: 186.6 nats; over the FULL 1704-decision span: 19.3 / 235.1 nats. Vacuous at every horizon the goalposts use; it only guarantees growth-rate convergence at rate (m ln T)/T, i.e. 15.4/365 = 4.2% per DAY of allowed shortfall in year one. ONS is O(m^1.5 log(mT)) (Agarwal et al. 2006 via Li–Hoi survey) and needs bounded price-relative ratios — crypto single-day moves of ±50% blow the constant. (2) Hedge/EWA over K=6 experts, losses in a range of width L: R_T ≤ L·sqrt(T·ln K/2) = 18.08·L (T=365). Trend-book daily σ_d ≈ 3.2% (from PARITY: ×21.69 @8bp over 4.67 y ⇒ log-growth 0.66/yr, Sharpe 1.09 ⇒ σ ≈ 0.61/yr; trader/backtest.py:464-471). L = ±3σ_d = 0.06 ⇒ regret ≤ 108% of NAV/yr = 1.89 annualised-Sharpe points; L=0.10 ⇒ 3.16; L=0.30 (crypto tail) ⇒ 9.5. Second-order bound (Cesa-Bianchi–Mansour–Stoltz 2007): R_T ≲ sqrt(2·ln K·Σ_t ℓ_t²) ⇒ in annualised-Sharpe units sqrt(2 ln K)·sqrt(365/T) = 1.89 (1 y), 1.34 (2 y), 0.88 (FULL 1704 d), 0.60 (10 y). The spread it must resolve: trend net@21 by year +1.69/+0.97/+0.89/−0.13/+0.55/−1.89 (2021…2026H1), UCRP +1.02/−2.49/+1.12/−0.24/−1.99/−2.45, flat 0 ⇒ best-minus-worst expert 1.5–3.5 Sharpe/yr, i.e. the same order as the guarantee. (3) The binding limit is statistical, not adversarial: SE of an annualised Sharpe over Y years ≈ sqrt((1+S²/2)/Y) (Lo 2002); SE of the DIFFERENCE between two tactics with correlation ρ: sqrt(2(1−ρ)(1+S²/2)/Y). S≈0.5: ρ=0 ⇒ 1.50 (Y=1), 0.67 (Y=5), 0.47 (Y=10); ρ=−0.3 (trend vs reversal) ⇒ 1.71 / 0.76 / 0.54. A 1.0-Sharpe gap between tactics is < 1 SE inside a year and reaches t=2 only after ≈9–12 stationary years ⇒ regret weights move on noise ⇒ forecast-combination puzzle (Stock–Watson 2004; Smith–Wallis 2009; DeMiguel–Garlappi–Uppal 2009: 3000 months for 25 assets). (4) Excess growth rate (Fernholz): γ* = ½(Σ_i w_i σ_i² − σ_p²). Inputs (assumed, to be measured): σ_i = 0.90/yr, mean pairwise ρ = 0.55, n = 64 EW ⇒ σ_p² = 0.81·(1/64 + (63/64)·0.55) = 0.451, σ_p = 0.672, γ* = 0.179/yr. Daily-rebalance turnover ≈ sqrt(2/π)·σ_idio,d = 0.798·sqrt(0.359/365) = 0.025/day ⇒ 21 bp cost = 0.025·0.0021·365 = 1.9%/yr ⇒ net γ* ≈ 0.16/yr ≈ +0.27 Sharpe on σ_p — relative to buy-and-hold of the SAME basket, not to cash. (5) Convex-hull bound: a simplex mixture returns Σ_k w_{t,k} r_{t,k}; E[Sharpe] ≤ Sharpe of the best fixed mixture in hindsight; two uncorrelated experts each S give (S1+S2)/√2, so clearing +0.97 by diversification alone needs ≥2 low-correlation experts each ≥ 0.97/√2 = 0.69 on the unseen years — the record has none (trend 2024–26H1 ≈ +0.1 avg, UCRP negative, flat 0). (6) Meta-layer cost: |Δw_k| ≤ η per step; theory η = sqrt(8 ln K/T) = 0.198 (T=365) ⇒ worst-case extra turnover 0.2 NAV/day ⇒ 0.2·21 bp·365 = 15%/yr on top of the experts' 0.155/day (11.9%/yr); FTL hard switches are lumpy (up to 2·gross per switch).

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: Every guarantee in the family is RELATIVE: UP/EG/ONS vs the best constant-rebalanced portfolio in hindsight; Hedge/Fixed-Share vs the best expert or best k-switch sequence. If cash/flat is in the class the hindsight target in a bear is ≥ 0, but the bound over BEAR22 (n=416 decisions, trader/config.py:70-78) is ((m−1)/2)·ln 417 ≈ 15 nats for m=6 — vacuous — and Hedge's slack of ≈1.9 annualised-Sharpe points exceeds the whole bear-year spread between experts. Adaptation is by cumulative past loss, so the weight entering 2022 sits on the 2021 winners (trend +1.69, UCRP +1.02 net@21) and UCRP alone then prints −2.49 (898 by-year, decay_trading_fixture.json). The meta is BEAR-positive only if it already holds a BEAR-positive expert, and the only measured BEAR-positive expert is the long-short trend book (+0.99 net@21 BEAR22) whose bear profit came entirely from the short side — a forecast property (the long-flat variant read −2.59 in BEAR22; 898 row, LEDGER.md:103). The rebalancing premium (≈+0.16–0.27 Sharpe-equivalent) is an add-on to a long-only basket that lost −2.49; it cannot flip the sign. A market-neutral constant-mix (long EW alts / short BTC) is beta-free by construction but its 2022 sign is an alt-vs-BTC risk-premium bet (alts underperformed), not a guarantee. Cuchiero–Schachermayer–Wong 2019 is explicit that the UP result is about ASYMPTOTIC growth-rate equality — nothing about finite windows or drawdowns.

controllability: Strongest 'hold on policy' of any family on the table: the deployable state is a K-vector on the simplex (K=6), every expert is a closed-form rule with a one-line definition, the meta's move each day is a deterministic function of a public loss ledger (Hedge: w_k ∝ exp(−η·L_k); FTL: argmax trailing Sharpe), so 'why did the book change' is answerable in one row. Turnover of the meta layer is bounded a priori (|Δw_k| ≤ η per step; with η=0.198 that is ≤0.2 NAV/day worst case, typically far less; FTL is lumpy but countable), the expert layer's turnover is the known 0.155/day, and the combined book stays gross ≤ 1 with no leverage, no HOLD-collapse mode (collapse to the flat expert is visible as w_flat → 1 and can be capped), and no hidden state. What is lost: (i) the layer cannot create edge — E[Sharpe] ≤ best fixed mixture of experts minus regret, so with the experts in the record (trend ≈ +0.1 avg 2024–26H1, UCRP < 0, flat 0) the ceiling is below the +0.56 PIT bar before any learning; (ii) adaptation speed ∝ 1/sqrt(T): a regime the length of BEAR22 (416 decisions) is not tracked within itself — Fixed-Share pays k·ln(T/k) per switch; (iii) the guarantees assume long-only multiplicative wealth — with shorts in the expert set UP/EG/ONS lose their framework (Hedge over expert RETURNS survives, UP over expert price relatives survives only while 1+r_k > 0 daily, true here for gross ≤ 1 books); (iv) the mean-reversion OLPS members are the opposite of controllable (turnover 1–2×/day, PAMR maxDD 96% even at zero fee) and must be excluded, not tamed; (v) with K experts and ~365 rounds the weights are statistically indistinguishable from noise around 1/K (Sharpe-difference SE ≈1.5/yr), so the 'audit' is of a random walk on the simplex.

Reasoning: (i) the convex-hull bound — the meta cannot beat the best fixed mixture of its experts in expectation, and the measured experts cap that hull: trend net@21 −0.13/+0.55/−1.89 on 2024/2025/2026H1, UCRP −0.24/−1.99/−2.45, flat 0; reaching +0.97 needs ≥2 low-correlation experts ≥ +0.69 each on those years and none exists, so the odds ride entirely on the never-measured daily reversal7 expert, which is a forecast and whose minute-scale cousins are cost-bound (813, 897); (ii) realised regret of Hedge on near-stationary experts typically costs 0.2–0.5 Sharpe vs the best expert and the worst-case bound is 0.9–1.9, both of the same order as the inter-expert spread; (iii) the external record is uniform: every non-cost-aware OLPS → 0.00 wealth at 0.25% on 10/10 fresh S&P portfolios (Moon et al. 2019), classical OLPS ≤ UCRP 0.86 Sharpe on crypto 2020–23 at zero fee with 79–96% drawdowns (arXiv 2512.08124), and the UCRP itself is −2.49 in 2022 on this panel; (iv) the repo's own two 'tactic hedging' reads are negative (lookback ensemble −0.16; inverse-vol −0.06) and its only regime switch (820 DD throttle) reduced drawdown without a recorded Sharpe gain. The one thing this row buys with high probability is a cheap, pre-registered closure of the 'hunt tactics not alpha' idea on the daily surface — plus a first honest number for a daily reversal book.
open_doubts: A daily equal-weight reversal book (E3) on the PIT panel at net@21 has never been measured; 813/897 tested minute-scale and 4-day triggers with n=6–25 hold-outs. If it reads ≥ +0.7 uncorrelated with trend on 2024–26 the hull argument weakens — but that would be a forecast finding belonging to the alpha family, not a tactic finding.

The regret numbers are worst-case bounds; realised regret of Hedge on i.i.d.-like experts is far smaller (often ≈ best expert − 0.1–0.3 Sharpe). The kill measures realised regret; the bounds only show the GUARANTEE is uninformative at T ≤ 2000.

Blum–Kalai 1999's exact commission-scaled constant was not verified (Springer paywalled); only the order (sublinear, O(m ln T)) is cited via the Li–Hoi survey text. Lo 2002's SE formula is from memory.

The EGR arithmetic uses assumed σ_i = 0.9 and mean pairwise ρ = 0.55 for 64 Kraken assets; the kill should print measured N_eff and ρ per year. If ρ is lower in 2024–26 the rebalancing premium is larger (still an add-on to a negative long-only base).

The scorer's `bh` is UCRP in log-return approximation (Σ w·Δlog p, not log Σ w·p_t+1/p_t); the second-order difference is ≈ ½·σ_idio,d² ≈ 5 bp/day — small but it is exactly the excess-growth term, so an EGR read from `bh` must recompute with simple returns.

Mixing opposite books nets trades inside the combined position matrix (a real source-4 saving); the scorer credits it automatically, but this also means a PASS could partly be cost-netting between trend and reversal — the SPEC should print expert-level vs combined turnover to attribute it.

K=6 with Hedge's theory η assumes T=365 rounds; a continuous multi-year run with a fixed η is not the anytime-optimal setting (η_t ∝ 1/sqrt(t) or Fixed-Share is); pre-registering three η values covers this but a 'doubling trick' variant was not included.

Short-side experts break UP/EG/ONS's long-only framework; UP over expert price relatives is valid only while every expert's daily 1+r_k > 0, which gross ≤ 1 books satisfy except in a > −100% day — fine here but should be asserted in code.
